items.heading: Greeting with Namaste (joining palms)
details: Touching all fingertips together activates pressure points linked to the eyes, ears, and mind, said to help you remember the person for a long time.
The slight bow and folded palms also keep a respectful distance, historically limiting the spread of germs through contact.

items.heading: Touching elders' feet (Charan Sparsh / Pada Namaskar)
details: The gesture is an exercise in humility and gratitude, helping reduce the ego.
Bending down and rising again is a small daily stretch that improves flexibility over time, and it reinforces respect between generations.

items.heading: Standing up to greet elders and guests
details: A small, near-universal sign of respect and attentiveness that also gets people up and moving through the day.

items.heading: Seeking elders' blessings
details: Encourages regular intergenerational interaction and social support within the family.

items.heading: Atithi Satkar / Hospitality
details: Strengthens reciprocal social relationships and builds a wider community support network.

items.heading: Community feasts (Bhoj)
details: Combine food sharing with social connection, strengthening ties within a community.

items.heading: Annadanam (food charity)
details: Provides food and social support to those in need within a community.

items.heading: Joint-family support systems
details: Allow childcare, eldercare, and household responsibilities to be shared across generations.

items.heading: Traditional Seva / community service
details: Encourages regular community participation and cooperation.

items.heading: Breaking a coconut before starting something new
details: The coconut is seen as a symbol of the ego - hard on the outside, pure and sweet within - broken to mark a fresh, humble start.
Sharing the broken pieces afterward is a small act of community and gratitude.
